answer: To curb Sybil attacks among maritime agents deployed from a shoreline jetty to a cliff summit, the network enforces hardware-rooted remote attestation. Each agent must execute within a certified secure enclave to sign telemetry from its navigation lantern. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of procuring physical cryptoprocessors per fake identity. However, microarchitectural side-channel exploits can extract enclave keys, allowing an adversary to clone multiple virtual agents.
